newsitem.title: USA: Shalala meets with health leaders on tobacco deal.
newsitem.headline: Shalala meets with health leaders on tobacco deal.

text.p: Leading public health advocates headed for the White House on Friday for the first in a series of meetings on the $368.5 billion settlement that states reached with tobacco companies.
The public health officials, including representatives from the American Lung Association and the American Cancer Society, were meeting to help craft recommendations for President Bill Clinton.

The representatives indicated that their concerns were in line with those raised by Clinton on Wednesday when he faulted the tobacco settlement plan for unreasonably restricting the government's ability to regulate nicotine.
Jonathan Fielding of the Partnership for Prevention said there was "virtual agreement" at the meeting on two points.

"The FDA (Food and Drug Administration) must have the authority to regulate tobacco as (it does) other drugs and devices, and secondly, the penalties for not meeting targets for smoking reduction are insufficient and need to be strengthened so that the industry has strong disincentives to continue to seduce youth to smoke," he said.
Recommendations for Clinton are expected within "weeks, not months," White House domestic policy adviser Bruce Reed said.

Reed and Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala head a presidential task force conducting a 30-day review of the proposed settlement between the tobacco industry and 40 U.S. states that have sued the industry.
